name: Prize crossword No 25,496
preamble: Five 4 of the 19 appear as solutions, not further defined in their clues; nor are 4 and 19. The other two are hidden in the grid, one of them in two places.

clue.text: 15 followed gold blocks

indicators.note: to block a passage is to sit inside it, so one piece lodges within the other

blocks.note: to tail someone is to follow them
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone trailed a precious metal that was blocking the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is ADAPTED, the answer at 15-across, standing in as the definition. 'Gold blocks' reads as bars of bullion, but gold is OR sitting inside the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tailored has been altered or cut to suit a particular purpose, which is exactly what adapted means.

clue.text: Superior pigment?

blocks.note: first meaning: Superior is a proper name here, the largest freshwater body on the US-Canada border, so this is a definition by example
second meaning: a pigment made by fixing a dye onto an insoluble mineral base

explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior pigment' looks like a top-quality paint; the capital S is hidden at the start of the clue, so Superior is the proper name. The question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Superior is one of the Great Lakes, and in painting a lake is a dye bound to a mineral base to make colour.

clue.text: Nothing better than a good stuffing, if you're this?

definitions.text: Nothing better than a good stuffing, if you're this?

indicators.note: stuffing is packed inside something else, so these letters go into the middle of another word

blocks.note: mere means nothing more than, as in a mere child
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A cook's advice to a skinny guest: there is nothing like a good stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, since a thin person would welcome a good feed, and also the wordplay: A G stuffed into a word meaning no more than.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre describes a person who is lean and underfed, someone who could do with a hearty meal.

clue.text: Conscientious objector looks threatening

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for conscientious objector
to lour (or lower) is to frown or look menacing, as a dark sky does

explanation.surface: A pacifist refusing to fight still manages to glower menacingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says this answer is not defined in its clue, so the whole clue is wordplay. It is the 4 of the 19: the colours of the rainbow, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the meaning: the seven hues of the spectrum are the theme set, and this word names those hues as a group.

clue.text: King hit Home Office and German government welcoming party

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for the Home Office, the UK interior ministry
und is the German word for and
a do is a party, such as a reception held to welcome guests
G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A monarch strikes at the Home Office and at the German government, which is greeting a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is Elvis Presley, the King of Rock and Roll, not a monarch, and 'hit' is a hit record rather than a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hound Dog was one of Elvis Presley's biggest chart successes, released in 1956 and covering a Big Mama Thornton song.

clue.text: Drunk rebel cases the Monarch pub, looking for this?

definitions.text: Drunk rebel cases the Monarch pub, looking for this?

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about out of order, so these letters lurch into a new arrangement
to case something is to enclose it in a case, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword shorthand for the Queen
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A drunken rebel staking out the King's Head, hunting for one more drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a drunk in a pub might well be looking for the barrel of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer barrel is the cask a pub draws its ale from, just what a thirsty drinker is after.

clue.text: Check about 10 litres

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes around what follows

blocks.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
the digits 1 and 0 written as the letters I and O
L is the abbreviation for litres

explanation.surface: An inspector checks a measure of roughly ten litres.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says this colour of the rainbow is not defined in its clue, so the whole clue is wordplay. '10' looks like a quantity; read it as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the meaning: this is the seventh band of the spectrum, the purple hue at the inner edge of the arc.

clue.text: British government went in to save battered old city?

indicators.note: going into something puts it inside, so one piece enters the other
something battered has been knocked out of shape, so these letters are knocked about

blocks.note: the Raj was British rule in India
taken as written, to be rearranged
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: British troops went in to rescue a war-ravaged ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the siege of the Bosnian capital in the 1990s, which is why the question mark is apt: the city really was battered.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarajevo is the capital city of Bosnia and Herzegovina, besieged for nearly four years during the Bosnian war.

clue.text: Gallic stonemason's award, almost the 60th

blocks.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
LIX is Roman 59, one short of LX, sixty

explanation.surface: A French mason receives an honour, nearly at his sixtieth birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The 60th' sounds like an anniversary, but it is a Roman numeral count: 'almost' it is the 59th, LIX.
explanation.definitionFit: Obelix, the Gaulish sidekick of Asterix in the French comics, carves and delivers menhirs, the standing stones of his village.

clue.text: Ball used to appear in odd places

indicators.note: odd places are the first, third, fifth and so on, so only those positions are kept

blocks.note: the letters in the odd-numbered positions of these two words

explanation.surface: A ball that was once used now turns up in strange spots.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says this colour of the rainbow is not defined, so the whole clue is wordplay. 'Odd places' sounds like strange locations; it means positions one, three, five and seven.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the meaning: this is the fifth band of the spectrum, the hue of a clear daytime sky.

clue.text: Bullet loaded in Luger illegally, breaking it?

definitions.text: Bullet loaded in Luger illegally, breaking it?

indicators.note: a cartridge loaded into a gun goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other
doing something illegally means not doing it properly, so these letters are set out improperly

blocks.note: a round is a single bullet or cartridge
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone illegally loads a round into a Luger, the German pistol, and asks if that is against the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: loading a gun illegally breaks a basic rule, and 'it' is that rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground rule is a basic principle governing conduct, the kind of rule that illegal acts break.

clue.text: Circle Line

blocks.note: O is round, so it stands for a circle
a range is a line, as in a mountain range

explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but the colour is undefined, per the preamble, and the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the meaning: this is the second band of the spectrum, sitting between red and yellow, named after the citrus fruit.

clue.text: Sort of code new police set about operating after an uprising

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so these letters take a fresh order
to be set about something is to be placed around it, so one piece encloses another
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
after means coming later, so this piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged
a machine that is operating is on

explanation.surface: A new police force goes into action after an uprising, with a fresh legal code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' sounds like the rebellion that prompts new policing, but it simply turns two letters upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Napoleonic Code is the French civil law system of 1804, so Napoleonic names one particular kind of legal code.

clue.text: In other versions, pilot starred with female

indicators.note: to pilot is to steer, so these letters are steered into a new course

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: In alternative editions of a film, the pilot was cast alongside a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' looks like a TV pilot episode or the aviator who starred; it is the instruction to steer the letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: Redrafts are rewritten texts, revised drafts that stand as alternative versions of an earlier document.

clue.text: A priest wore outmoded suit in the past

indicators.note: what is worn goes round the wearer, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
dated means old-fashioned
P is the abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman used to wear an old-fashioned suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like the clothing he wore, but the definition is the verb suit, put in the past tense: suited.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit something to a purpose is to adjust it to fit, so suited in the past tense is a synonym of altered to fit.

clue.text: Fancy roast venison I nicked?

indicators.note: roasting cooks meat into a different state, so these letters are worked over
something nicked is pocketed, tucked away inside, so this letter goes within the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to pinching a joint of roast venison for a fancy dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the roast, but it is the verb: to imagine.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something in the old sense is to picture it in the mind, which is what envisioning means.

clue.text: Dish of burnished regal gold a duke dumped

indicators.note: what is dumped is thrown away, so these letters are taken out
burnished metal has been worked and polished, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, then removed
D is the abbreviation for duke, removed

explanation.surface: A platter of polished royal gold was thrown out by a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one A and the D from the nine letters, then rearrange the seven left.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg roll is a Chinese-American fried snack, a filled pastry roll served as a dish or starter.

clue.text: Cover over unit is bound to be put on a pedestal

indicators.note: a cover laid over something closes around it, so one piece encloses the rest
something bound is tied up inside, so these letters are held within another word

blocks.note: a lid is a cover
one is a single unit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A covered unit is certain to be raised up on a plinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as certain to be, but 'bound' works on its own: one word ties up the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise someone is to treat them as a celebrity, idolising them as people do a hero raised up for admiration.

clue.text: Gunmen in part of east London

blocks.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
taken as written
Bow is a district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: Armed men are spotted in a district in the east of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble leaves this answer undefined, so the whole clue is wordplay. 'In' looks like a container signal, but it simply stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the meaning: this is the arc of spectral colours formed when sunlight is refracted through raindrops, the puzzle's theme.

clue.text: When swimming, five catch virus — one pongs

indicators.note: a swimmer's limbs thrash every which way, so these letters move about freely
to catch something is to take hold of it, so one piece grips another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
flu, influenza, is a virus
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Five swimmers pick up a bug, and one of them smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pongs' looks like a verb, but it is the plural noun; pong is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluvia are unpleasant vapours or odours given off by something, so they are stenches or bad smells.

clue.text: Pretends to be from abroad or leaving Sweden

indicators.note: what is leaving goes away, so those letters depart from the word

blocks.note: foreign means from another country
taken as written, then removed
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Someone poses as a foreigner, or else as an emigrant from Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a conjunction offering an alternative; it is two letters to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to put on a false show of something, which is what someone who pretends does.

clue.text: React to sudden pain

blocks.note: to yell is to cry out, a way of reacting
ow is the exclamation of sudden pain

explanation.surface: How to respond when something suddenly hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble leaves this colour undefined, so the clue is all wordplay, and the surface is literally true: one yells 'ow'.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the meaning: this is the third band of the spectrum, the hue of lemons and egg yolks.

clue.text: They always approve head of state in Arab country

indicators.note: being in a place means being inside it, so one letter goes within the other word
the head is the top or front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: Yemen is a country in the Arabian peninsula
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Courtiers nod through every decision of an Arab nation's ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of state' sounds like a president or monarch, but it is the first letter of the word state.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are sycophants who agree with whatever a superior says, never voicing any objection.

clue.text: In over half of Limoges its factories make cars

indicators.note: a little more than half is kept, so the tail of the word is cut away

blocks.note: the first four of its seven letters
usines is French for factories, apt for a French city

explanation.surface: In more than half the plants of Limoges, the French porcelain city, workers build cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' signals that the factories belong to a French city, so the word is in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Limousines are large luxurious motor vehicles, chauffeur-driven saloons with a partition behind the driver.

clue.text: In Paris who's first to devalue our cash?

indicators.note: first means the opening position, so only the initial letter is kept

blocks.note: qui is French for who
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A worried question: who in France is the first to debase our money?
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is British slang for a pound sterling, hence 'our' in a British puzzle; 'who's' is read as 'who is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quid is informal British slang for one pound, the unit of money used in the setter's own country.

clue.text: Treat this serpentine to make quartzite grill

indicators.note: serpentine means winding like a snake, so the letters twist into another shape

blocks.note: taken as written, added to the answer before mixing
the answer itself, joined to the other letters
the result of the mixing, from which the extra letters are subtracted

explanation.surface: A geology instruction: heat this snaking stone to turn it into quartzite.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the five letters of the first word plus the answer rearrange to give the rock, so take those five letters out of the rock to leave the answer. Serpentine is also a mineral, which feeds the geology surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to question them intensely, and to quiz them is to put questions to them.

clue.text: Model doing without this writer

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece sits outside the other
to model is to shape clay, so these letters are moulded into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the setter writing the clue refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: A fashion model manages fine without the columnist.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble leaves this colour undefined. 'Without' looks like it removes the writer, but in its old sense it means outside, so the letter is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the meaning: this is the sixth band of the spectrum, a deep blue-violet named after a plant dye from India.

clue.text: Web addict swallows drug (crack)

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: an onliner is someone who spends their time on the internet
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An internet junkie takes some crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'crack' looks like the name of the drug; it is the definition, a crack being a wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack in the sense of a wisecrack is a quick witty remark, and a one-liner is a short joke.
